target.host: Mac Studio M1 Ultra, 128 GB unified memory, internal SSD, macOS 26.0

termination.fault: the paged loader built the processor without eos ids, so the stopping set held only 154820 <|endoftext|>; mlx-vlm stream_generate does not reset it from the config; generations ran past 154827 <|user|> to max_tokens
termination.correction: install the checkpoint config's declared eos ids [154820, 154827, 154829] after verifying each is a control token; identical in both arms of every comparison
termination.caveat: the literal text <|user|> also encodes to 154827
termination.real_model_regression: 3 historical prompts: natural termination in 7/5/11 tokens, pre-terminal greedy prefixes identical to history

definitions.request_latency_s: server: submit -> completion (after model load); reference: generate() wall time of a fresh process with an empty store, after its load
definitions.ratio: persistent request latency / reference request latency, paired within a block
definitions.result_records: stream result records from mlx-vlm stream_generate; under finish=length the last record repeats the final token (N records = N-1 decode steps); under finish=stop the last record is the terminal token
definitions.decode_tps: (records-1) / (time of last record - time of first record)
definitions.gain_rule: ratio <= 0.95 in every one of >= 3 blocks; the block maximum is reported
definitions.identity: greedy token ids identical between arms through the terminal boundary (after the record normalization)

retained_across_requests: expert slot tensors and their logical map
fresh_per_request: prompt cache (KV, sparse-attention, recurrent and convolution state)

warm_store_g57.identity: all paired strata identical in all blocks
warm_store_g57.strata_note: values are per block 1/2/3 from warm-store-results.json; persistent strata named explicitly (cold-first = first request on an empty logical store; repeat = immediate exact repeat; unrelated-M = M after S); reference = fresh process with an empty store

confirmation_g60.prompts: disjoint from G57 and all earlier sets
confirmation_g60.invalid: blocks 1-3 sustained-512: the client ran 128 tokens instead of 512 (plan bug); kept, labelled, rerun as blocks 4-6

quality_g58.suite: SYNTHETIC fresh sealed suite r3: 120 units, 5 domains x 24, 108 problem groups, frozen before any run; prompt tokens 27-121; max_tokens 256; effort low; greedy
quality_g58.reference: fresh paged process per task, empty store
quality_g58.candidate: one cold-started persistent process over the sealed order
quality_g58.retention_lower_bound_method: exact one-sided binomial (Clopper-Pearson) over independent reference-success groups: 0.05^(1/107)
quality_g58.scope: scope-limited relative retention of the persistent candidate vs the fresh-process paged reference on this synthetic suite; not general accuracy, not a certification of the base model or of the quantization against a higher-precision checkpoint; grouping does not establish representativeness
quality_g58.mixed_warm_subset: 20 tasks after priming with M on the same process: 20/20 identical to the sealed-order outputs

segment_1.schedule: frozen: 6 h or 240 requests, whichever first; 15-step cycle (13 requests + 60 s and 120 s idles)
segment_1.latency_drift: first-half vs second-half medians equal per stratum

segment_2.schedule: amended before the run: 6 h duration cap, request cap 400, same cycle and checks

soak_g59.usability_note: the client required a usable answer only for S, B, S_append, S_edit, SENTINEL and SLOWCLIENT_S; process/lifecycle health and answer usability are reported separately; M's 0 usable answers are a property of the frozen 128-token workload at reasoning effort low, recorded before the soak

sentinel.prompt: What is 17 times 6? Answer with the number only.

lifecycle_g56.cancel: client disconnect releases the worker in 0.5 s; following requests identical
lifecycle_g56.queue: 4 accepted (identical outputs) / 2 rejected 503 overloaded at 6 concurrent
lifecycle_g56.slow_consumer: server completes independently of client read pace
lifecycle_g56.poisoned_store: engine not ready, 503 on new requests, no automatic reload (fake-model test; no real poisoning occurred)

budget_70e9.status: ADMITTED 2026-09-20 as the recommended expert budget for this configuration on this host (flag change, reversible); nothing deployed. Supersedes the 60e9 configuration block above for new runs; every other section of this file remains a 60e9 record.

definitions.expert_cache_bytes: the slot store's byte budget; capacity_per_layer = floor(budget / (42 layers x 14,155,776 B per expert))
definitions.decode_misses_per_token: store misses charged to decode steps only (prefill misses excluded), divided by decode steps
definitions.decode_ratio: 70e9 decode_tps_last_half / 60e9 decode_tps_last_half, paired within a block on the same prompt
definitions.total_latency_ratio: 70e9 total request latency / 60e9 total request latency, paired
definitions.peak_delta_bytes: 70e9 peak MLX memory minus 60e9 peak MLX memory for the same prompt in the same block
definitions.min_free_gib: minimum host free memory sampled by the run watchdog during the run
definitions.identity: greedy token id lists identical between the two budgets for the same prompt in the same block

latency_context_not_a_gate.summary: 10-13 % lower request latency on every stratum

caveats: soak exposure 80 requests / 1.33 h at 70e9 vs 335 requests / 6.03 h at 60e9; the 6 h segment at 70e9 has not run, so no production-shaped claim is made at 70e9

macOS un-wires the MLX buffers while the server is idle (wired ~83.5 -> ~3.09 GiB in idle samples, rising again on the next request); pages stay resident and the compressor stays flat - accounting, not release - and the same pattern is present at 60e9

paged_reference.py at 971db9c1 pins its admitted ceiling at 60e9 inside verify_artifact and refuses a 70e9 budget with EXPERT_CACHE_OVER_BUDGET, so the 70e9 fresh-process reference ran through run_offload.py (same loader, same store, same stop policy, byte-identical prompts); the ceiling becomes an explicit --max-expert-cache-bytes flag in a separate commit

streaming_prefill_negative.hypothesis: run the prefill pass outside the slot store (--prefill-mode stream: read each wave's experts as transients, run the same three gather_qmm calls, drop them) and spend the reclaimed memory on slots
streaming_prefill_negative.verdict: NO GAIN under the frozen gates; retained on its branch, default-off, not a candidate
streaming_prefill_negative.memory: PASS - peak transient 3,385,655,296 B against a 4.0e9 B gate; store counters undisturbed (delta hits/misses/evictions/read_bytes 0)
streaming_prefill_negative.identity: FAIL - 3 of 6 prompts diverge; a layer differs exactly when its trailing stream wave holds fewer than 64 experts, because MLX's plain and sorted gather_qmm kernels are not bit-equal (max abs <= 0.125 in bf16, with argmax flips) and the baseline's slots.size >= 64 rule selects the sorted kernel where the short wave selects the plain one
streaming_prefill_negative.prefill: FAIL - gate was >= 1.5x, block max 0.763x; first token 15.6 -> 23.8 s on the short code prompt; the stream path reads the same unique-expert byte set the slot path reads (52.8 vs 54.2 GB) and overlaps no reads with compute
streaming_prefill_negative.end_to_end: FAIL - 1.07-1.32x slower; sustained decode unchanged (mean 1.003x); early decode 0.55-0.82x over the first 8 tokens because a streamed prefill admits nothing to the decode store
streaming_prefill_negative.stale_premise: with per-expert slot writes the baseline's own prefill transient at 60e9 is <= 2.6 GB, worth <= 4 slots per layer, so even a perfect stream prefill could not buy a meaningful budget increase
streaming_prefill_negative.residual_note: the baseline's kernel selection (do_sort = slots.size >= 64) means bit-identity is conditional on execution shape; any future path must reproduce it exactly

levers_that_do_not_reduce_io.speculative_union_batching: verifying k consecutive tokens in one forward pass, scored at the full-acceptance upper bound, needs the union of their experts: 13.8-14.1 of 16 per layer at k=2; misses/token 80.7 -> 79.3 at k=4. Top-8-of-288 routing leaves almost no overlap between adjacent tokens, so there is nothing to amortize.
levers_that_do_not_reduce_io.request_batching: two concurrent requests amortize 0.77-0.79, i.e. they produce more total misses than running one at a time

limitations: one host (M1 Ultra 128 GB); no M2 Max qualification
request limits: prompt <= 2048 tokens, max_tokens <= 512, queue 4, one generation at a time
synthetic checks and synthetic task suite
OS page cache observed, not controlled; no independently measured physical SSD bytes (counters are logical/requested bytes)
the 149-token M prompt is not long-context coverage
the request deadline cancels at the next token; a stall before the first token is not interrupted by it (dead-worker detection and the memory watchdog cover the process)

decode ~2.6-3.3 tokens/s in both arms at the 60e9 budget: it holds ~35 % of the ~170 GB expert corpus, so decode is miss-bound and persistence shortens prefill only; the admitted 70e9 budget holds ~41 % and lifted paired CLI decode to 3.06-4.20 tokens/s (see budget_70e9), which does not change the miss-bound character
no deployment authorization; the candidate never replaced the default service
transformation: values copied by hand from the private JSON records named above (no numeric transformation except rounding as shown); the lower bound is recomputed by g58_score.py's lower_bound()
